text:
maria: quick follow-up from the shim RFC — we need a concrete plan for metric/telemetry for adapter-layer fallbacks. not just ‘log it’, we need per-tenant visibility and an easy way to query rollback candidates.

ken: +1. customers will ask for "observability" during migration windows. proposing: tenant-scoped counters (shim_hit, shim_fallback, shim_latency_p95) + sample traces for fallback flows.

sasha: agree on counters. want to add a dimension: client_version header so we can correlate which SDKs trigger shim behavior. without that it's hard to target comms.

maria: exactly — plan: 1) tag requests at ingress with client.version 2) increment shim_* counters on decision 3) emit trace with decision tree when fallback happens (keep sample rate low).

ria: question about storage/retention: do we put these in existing metrics pipeline (Prom/Tempo) or a separate index for quick tenant lookups? cost implications matter.

ken: put counters in Prom, histograms for latency. For traces, use sampled traces in Tempo. For tenant lookups we can add a short-lived per-tenant time-series label (tenant_id) and a 30d retention. full traces kept 7d.

maria: policy: default sampling 1% for traces, ramp to 10% for tenants hitting >1% fallback rate. We should also emit a lightweight per-tenant daily rollup (fallback_count, total_requests, fallback_ratio) to BigQuery/analytics for dashboards.

ria: bigquery sounds good for dashboards. who owns the rollup job? eng-sre or infra-analytics?

sasha: infra-analytics should own the ETL but runtime needs to add the export hook. I can add a Flink job proto if infra-analytics agrees.

ken: ops note: must avoid PII leaks — ensure tenant_id is a stable hashed id and no prompt content in traces. traces should only include decision metadata and timing.

maria: agreed. also: add a boolean header shim_applied to responses for clients who opt-in to see when shim was used. This helps SDKs surface behavior to developers. opt-in only.

ria: opt-in header raises compliance questions for enterprise customers — need feature flag to disable header globally per org.

sasha: we can gate via tenant feature flag. default off for enterprise, on for internal testing tenants.

maria: rollout plan: canary 5% traffic with metrics + alert if fallback_ratio > 0.5% OR p95 latency increases > 20ms. After 48h, increase to 25% if no regressions.

ken: add an SLO dashboard tile: fallback_ratio by tenant, p95 delta vs baseline, and CPU/GPU allocation for shim routing. Also an on-call runbook snippet: "if fallback_ratio spikes, flip routing to safer model variant and open incident."

ria: can we backfill historical client_version? we didn't capture it before.

sasha: not reliably. we'll start capturing from rollout, but we can infer some with SDK telemetry when available.

maria: actionable TODOs: @sasha implement header tagging + shim counters (PR by Fri), @ken create prometheus alert rules + dashboard (by Mon), @ria coordinate retention & BigQuery ETL (sync with infra-analytics). I'll draft the rollout playbook and runbook.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime/adapter-metrics v1.2 -> staging (started) :rocket:

maria: thanks — keep updates here. also please add a short example snippet for SDKs to emit client.version so we can correlate.

ken: snippet: ```http
GET /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer ...
Client-Version: sdk-js/3.1.0
```

maria: perfect. we'll include that in the rollout notes. :thumbsup:

ria: one more: export a one-line CSV daily with tenant, fallback_ratio, sample_traces_link for support to triage customer asks. low effort and very helpful.

sasha: good idea. infra-analytics — can you take that on?

maria: wrapping up — main constraints: minimal perf overhead, no sensitive data in traces, tenant-scoped visibility, opt-in headers, and clear alert thresholds. if anyone sees a missing piece call it out now.

ken: nothing else from me. excited to get this running.

ria: sounds good. will sync with infra-analytics tomorrow.

sasha: starting the PR this afternoon.
